title: AOM Brand Guidelines v2
summary: Core AOM brand guidelines synced to the live site, for all agents building AOM work.
content:
AOM Brand Guidelines

Version 2.0 | Steffen (SS) | Updated 2026-03-12 (synced to live site) For Bobby, Cleo, Tony, and anyone building AOM-facing work.

1. Positioning

One-Line Positioning Statement

AOM builds the content, websites, and systems that make companies impossible to ignore.

Tagline Candidates

  1. "Brand infrastructure for companies that build." (lead candidate, construction-forward, works for all verticals)
  2. "The system behind the brand." (AI/systems angle, works as secondary tagline)
  3. "We make what moves you forward." (broader, warmer, good for general use)

Who AOM Is (One Paragraph)

AOM is a creative production and systems company based in Phoenix. We build the things that actually grow businesses: video that recruits and closes deals, websites that convert, social content that runs like a machine, and AI-powered workflows that make it all repeatable. We're not a video production company. We're the team that builds the engine behind your brand.

Who AOM Is NOT

  • Not a template shop
  • Not a freelancer collective
  • Not a "we do everything" agency
  • Not selling AI hype or chatbot demos
  • Not chasing trends. Building infrastructure.
  • Not corporate. Not scrappy either. Somewhere more intentional than both.

2. Color System

Philosophy

Dark foundation. Warm, not cold. The current site runs zinc/cool gray. We're shifting to a warmer neutral base that feels more human and more premium. Orange stays, but with restraint. The new sage green accent gives AOM a visual layer no competitor has.

Primary Palette

Role Name Hex Usage
Primary Accent AOM Orange #E85D26 CTAs, active states, emphasis moments. Never more than 10-15% of any screen.
AI Accent Sage #7C9A72 AI/systems section, status indicators, secondary highlights. The "growth" signal.
Gold Gold #C9A84C Premium accents, highlight moments, tier indicators.
Gold Light Gold Light #D4B85E Hover state on gold elements, lighter gold accents.

Background Colors (Dark Frame v4)

Role Name Hex Usage
Primary BG Night #0C0C0C Main page background.
Card BG (dark) Night Card #151515 Cards, modals, elevated surfaces on dark sections.
Card BG (legacy) Charcoal #141412 Legacy card background. Use night-card for new builds.
Surface BG Deep Warm #1A1A17 Section alternation, input fields, sidebar backgrounds.
Mid Dark Mid Dark #1A1A1A Alternative dark surface.
Black Black #0A0A0A True black for deepest layers.

Light Theme Colors (ServicesGrid and light sections)

Role Name Hex Usage
Cream Cream #FDF6EC Light-section backgrounds (ServicesGrid).
Cream Alt Cream Alt #F5EFE6 Alternate light backgrounds.
Cream Dark Cream Dark #EDE7DF Slightly darker cream for depth.
Light Border Light Border #D9D3CB Borders on light-section cards.

Text Colors

Role Name Hex Usage
Primary Text (v4) Text Light #F0ECE6 Headlines, primary body text on dark backgrounds. Preferred for new builds.
Primary Text (legacy) Warm White #F5F0EB Legacy alias. Still works in existing components.
Secondary Text Stone #7A7267 Subheadings, supporting copy. Warm gray.
Tertiary Text / Muted Text Muted #8A847C Captions, timestamps, micro-labels, metadata.
Legacy Muted Stone Muted #9A9189 Legacy alias for muted text in older components.
Legacy Dim Dim #A89F96 Legacy alias for dimmed text.

Accent and Utility Colors

Role Name Hex When to Use
Orange Hover Darker Orange #D14E1C Hover state on orange elements. Darker, not lighter (v4 direction).
Orange Muted Muted Orange #C44A1F Borders, subtle orange tints.
Orange Glow Ember #E85D26 at 10% opacity Glows, box-shadows, ambient light effects behind CTAs.
Sage Light Soft Sage #9BB593 Hover state on sage elements.
Sage Muted Deep Sage #5C7A54 Borders and subtle tints in AI sections.
Success Green #22C55E Form success states, confirmations.
Error Red #EF4444 Form errors, alerts.
Border (dark) Night Border rgba(255,255,255,0.10) Default borders on dark-section cards, dividers. Subtle white at 10%.
Border Hover (dark) Night Border Hover rgba(255,255,255,0.18) Hover state on dark-section bordered elements.
Border (legacy) Border #D9D3CB Legacy alias. Maps to light-border now.
Border Hover (legacy) Border Hover #C4BDB4 Legacy hover alias.

Tailwind Config

// tailwind.config.js — colors (synced to live site 2026-03-12)
export default {
  theme: {
    extend: {
      colors: {
        orange: { 600: '#E85D26' },
        aom: {
          // Bold Graphic v4 brand direction
          cream: '#FDF6EC',
          'cream-dark': '#EDE7DF',
          'cream-alt': '#F5EFE6',
          black: '#0A0A0A',
          orange: '#E85D26',
          'orange-hover': '#D14E1C',
          'orange-muted': '#C44A1F',
          gold: '#C9A84C',
          'gold-light': '#D4B85E',
          'warm-gray': '#7A7267',
          'light-border': '#D9D3CB',

          // Dark Frame system (v4)
          night: '#0C0C0C',
          'night-card': '#151515',
          'night-border': 'rgba(255,255,255,0.10)',
          'night-border-hover': 'rgba(255,255,255,0.18)',
          charcoal: '#141412',
          surface: '#1A1A17',
          'mid-dark': '#1A1A1A',
          'text-light': '#F0ECE6',
          'text-muted': '#8A847C',

          // Legacy aliases for components not yet refactored
          'warm-white': '#F5F0EB',
          stone: '#7A7267',
          'stone-muted': '#9A9189',
          dim: '#A89F96',
          border: '#D9D3CB',
          'border-hover': '#C4BDB4',

          // Accent
          sage: '#7C9A72',
          'sage-light': '#9BB593',
          'sage-muted': '#5C7A54',
        }
      },
      boxShadow: {
        'orange-glow': '0 0 30px rgba(232,93,38,0.15)',
        'orange-glow-lg': '0 0 60px rgba(232,93,38,0.2)',
      }
    }
  }
}

3. Typography

System Overview

Role Font Weight Style Size Line Height
Headlines Syne 800 (ExtraBold) Italic, uppercase 36-72px (responsive) 0.85-0.9
Subheadlines Syne 700 (Bold) Normal 18-24px 1.2
Body Space Grotesk 400 (Regular) Normal 16px (1rem) 1.6
Body Emphasis Space Grotesk 600 (SemiBold) Normal 16px 1.6
Micro Labels JetBrains Mono 700 (Bold) Normal 9-11px 1.2
AI/System Text JetBrains Mono 400 (Regular) Normal 13-14px 1.5
Stat Numbers Syne 800 (ExtraBold) Italic 48-72px 0.85

Font Sources

Syne (Headlines, Subheadlines, Stats)

  • Google Fonts: https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Syne
  • Import (index.html): https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Syne:wght@700;800;900
  • Import (index.css): @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Syne:wght@400;500;600;700;800&family=Space+Grotesk:wght@300;400;500;600;700&display=swap');
  • Note: Syne maxes out at ExtraBold (800). Use font-extrabold not font-black (900).

Space Grotesk (Body)

  • Google Fonts: https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Space+Grotesk
  • Import: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Space+Grotesk:wght@400;500;600

JetBrains Mono (Mono/System/AI Layer)

  • Google Fonts: https://fonts.google.com/specimen/JetBrains+Mono
  • Import: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;700

Tailwind Font Config

// tailwind.config.js — fontFamily (synced to live site 2026-03-12)
fontFamily: {
  headline: ['Syne', 'system-ui', 'sans-serif'],
  body: ['"Space Grotesk"', 'system-ui', 'sans-serif'],
  mono: ['"JetBrains Mono"', 'monospace'],
}

Typography Rules

  • Headlines are ALWAYS uppercase, italic, extrabold weight (800), tight tracking (tracking-tighter or letter-spacing: -0.02em)
  • Subheadlines are sentence case, bold weight, normal style
  • Body text minimum #7A7267 (stone) on dark backgrounds for readable body copy.
  • Micro-labels: uppercase, tracking-[0.3em], mono font, #8A847C (text-muted) or #9A9189 (stone-muted)
  • Line lengths: max 65ch for body text, max 45ch for headlines
  • No font sizes below 9px anywhere on the site

4. Visual Language

Photography Direction

  • Real shots only. No stock photography. Ever.
  • Color grading: Slightly desaturated, warm midtones, deep shadows. Think filmic, not Instagram filter. Shadows lean warm (not blue/teal).
  • Construction clients: Show real job sites, real crews, real equipment. Composition matters. Even an iPhone shot should feel intentional.
  • Corporate/event: Slightly editorial. Shallow depth of field for interviews. Wide establishing shots for scale.
  • Post-processing: Lift blacks slightly (not crushed), warm highlights, grain is acceptable and encouraged at subtle levels.

Icon Style

  • Lucide icons (already in the codebase). Consistent 18-20px size in UI.
  • Stroke weight: default (2px). Never filled.
  • Color: #7A7267 (stone) default, #E85D26 (orange) for active/accent states.
  • Icons inside containers: 40-48px square, border border-aom-night-border bg-black/40, icon centered.

Border and Divider Treatment

  • Borders (dark sections): 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.10) (aom-night-border). Subtle white transparency on dark.
  • Borders (light sections): 1px solid #D9D3CB (aom-light-border). Warm edge on cream backgrounds.
  • Dividers: same color as section border, full-width or inset depending on context
  • No rounded corners on primary containers. Use rounded-sm (2px) maximum. Squares feel more intentional.
  • Hover borders: transition to rgba(255,255,255,0.18) (night-border-hover) or #E85D26 at reduced opacity (border-aom-orange/30)
  • Cards get shadow-xl or shadow-2xl for depth on dark backgrounds
  • Orange glow shadows: shadow-orange-glow (30px) and shadow-orange-glow-lg (60px) for CTA emphasis

Spacing Philosophy

  • Generous vertical spacing between sections: py-24 minimum on desktop, py-16 on mobile
  • Interior card padding: p-8 minimum on desktop, p-6 on mobile
  • Component gaps: gap-6 between cards, gap-4 for tighter groupings
  • Let things breathe. White space (dark space, in our case) is a premium signal.
  • Headlines to content: mb-8 minimum

Animation Philosophy

  • What moves: Page entry (fade up, y: 30 to y: 0), hover states, scroll-triggered reveals, the scramble text effect on interactive elements
  • What doesn't move: Logos, navigation, body text. Nothing bounces. Nothing pulses except intentional loading states.
  • Timing: duration-300 for hovers, duration-700 for scroll reveals, duration-1000+ for hero entrance
  • Easing: Default ease-out. Never linear except for infinite loops (scroll ticker).
  • Rule: If it doesn't serve comprehension or delight, it doesn't animate.

Dark Mode Specifics

  • The site IS dark mode. There is no light mode toggle.
  • All colors are designed for dark backgrounds first.
  • Cream (#FDF6EC) is used for light-section backgrounds (ServicesGrid). Also available for exports (PDFs, proposals, print).
  • The noise/grain texture overlay stays: opacity-[0.03], fractalNoise, mix-blend-overlay. It adds analog warmth.
  • The subtle orange gradient wash stays: opacity-[0.02], bg-gradient-to-b from-transparent via-orange-500/5 to-transparent.

5. Component Patterns

Section Headers

Structure:
- Mono micro-label (category): uppercase, tracking-[0.3em], #8A847C (text-muted), 10px, JetBrains Mono Bold
- Headline: uppercase, italic, extrabold weight (800), Syne, tracking-tighter, #F0ECE6 (text-light)
- Optional subhead: sentence case, Space Grotesk 400, #7A7267 (stone), max-w-2xl
- Optional orange accent line: 48px wide, 2px tall, #E85D26, between label and headline

Example classes:
<p class="text-[10px] font-mono font-bold uppercase tracking-[0.3em] text-aom-text-muted mb-4">Our Work</p>
<h2 class="font-headline text-4xl md:text-6xl font-extrabold italic uppercase tracking-tighter text-aom-text-light">Portfolio</h2>
<p class="text-aom-stone text-base mt-4 max-w-2xl">The work speaks. Real clients, real results.</p>

Cards and Tiles

Standard Card (dark sections):

  • Background: bg-aom-night-card (#151515) or bg-aom-surface
  • Border: border border-aom-night-border
  • Padding: p-8
  • Corners: rounded-sm
  • Shadow: shadow-xl
  • Hover: hover:border-aom-night-border-hover transition-colors duration-300

Standard Card (light sections):

  • Background: bg-white
  • Border: border border-aom-light-border
  • Same padding/corners, hover shifts border darker

Accent Card (selected/featured):

  • Border: border-aom-orange/40
  • Background: bg-orange-950/10 (use Tailwind's built-in orange-950 with opacity)
  • Same padding and corners as standard

AI/Systems Card:

  • Border: border-aom-sage-muted/30
  • Background: bg-emerald-950/10
  • Mono font for labels inside
  • Sage accent color instead of orange

CTAs

Primary CTA:

  • Background: bg-aom-orange
  • Text: text-white font-headline font-extrabold uppercase tracking-tight
  • Padding: px-8 py-4
  • Hover: hover:bg-aom-orange-hover transition-colors
  • No border-radius. Square.
  • Shadow: shadow-lg shadow-aom-orange/20

Secondary CTA:

  • Background: transparent
  • Border: border border-aom-warm-white
  • Text: text-aom-text-light font-headline font-bold uppercase tracking-tight
  • Padding: px-8 py-4
  • Hover: hover:bg-aom-text-light hover:text-aom-night transition-all

Ghost CTA (inline/text links):

  • Text: text-aom-orange font-bold
  • No background, no border
  • Hover: hover:text-aom-orange-hover with optional underline
  • Arrow icon inline: <ArrowRight size={14} />

Services Grid

Structure: 3 columns on desktop, 1 column on mobile. Each tile represents a service lane.

Each tile contains:

  1. Icon container (48px square, bordered, icon inside at 20px)
  2. Mono micro-label with service category
  3. Headline (Syne Bold, not italic for tile titles)
  4. 1-2 sentence description in body text
  5. "Learn more" ghost CTA at bottom

The three lanes:

  1. Content Engine (retainer) -- Repeat icon, orange accent
  2. Production (project) -- Clapperboard icon, orange accent
  3. Digital Infrastructure (system) -- Cpu icon, sage accent

Case Study Cards

Structure:

  • Full-width or half-width image/video embed at top (aspect-video)
  • Below image: client name (mono micro-label), project title (headline style), one-line result metric in orange
  • Tags: small pill badges with category (same style as current video tags)
  • Hover: border shifts to orange, image slightly scales (group-hover:scale-105)

Required fields per case study:

  • Client name
  • Project type
  • Hero image or video embed
  • One quantifiable result
  • 2-3 tags

AI/Systems Visual Layer

This is how AOM communicates its AI and systems capability without saying "AI" in neon letters.

Visual cues:

  • JetBrains Mono is the AI voice. Any time the system is "speaking," it's in mono.
  • Sage green (#7C9A72) accents instead of orange in AI sections
  • Status-indicator styling: small dots (4-6px) that are sage green = active, #57534E = inactive
  • Process flows shown as labeled steps with mono text and connecting lines (not flowchart clip art)
  • Input/output framing: "1 filming day in. 30 days of content out." -- always show the transformation

What to avoid:

  • Gradient blobs
  • Robot/android imagery
  • Circuit board patterns
  • The word "AI" in headlines (use it in body copy sparingly)
  • ChatGPT-style chat bubble interfaces

What to show instead:

  • The dashboard or pipeline view (how the system actually works)
  • Real numbers and real outputs
  • Mono-typed system status labels
  • The "How It Works" section that reveals process without tech jargon

6. Voice

How AOM Talks to Construction Companies

  • Speak results, not production jargon. "Your best crews aren't on Indeed. They're on Instagram watching your competitor's content."
  • Reference what they care about: recruiting, winning bids, looking legitimate to general contractors, standing out from the sea of blue-and-orange logos.
  • Be direct. Construction people respect directness.
  • Show the gap: their current presence vs what's possible. Side-by-side is the most powerful sales tool.

How AOM Talks About AI

  • Show the system, not the technology.
  • Lead with the outcome: "We built a system that turns one filming day into 30 days of content." The AI is the how, not the what.
  • Never lead with "AI-powered" or "leveraging artificial intelligence." That's vendor speak.
  • Acceptable: "We built internal systems that..." / "The engine behind..." / "How the pipeline works"
  • The waitlist framing: "We built this for ourselves first. Now we're opening it up." Scarcity is real, not manufactured.

Words We Use

  • Build, ship, system, engine, pipeline, infrastructure
  • Real, intentional, repeatable, consistent
  • Impact, results, proof, output
  • Crew, team (not "resources" or "talent pool")

Words We Don't Use

  • Leverage, utilize, synergy, optimize (corporate rot)
  • Cutting-edge, revolutionary, disruptive (startup rot)
  • Content creator (we're producers and builders)
  • AI-powered, machine learning, neural network in headlines (backend jargon)
  • "Book a call" (use "See What We'd Build For You" or "Start a Brief")

Headline Formula

[Bold claim or result] + [who it's for or what it replaces]

Examples:

  • "Brand infrastructure for companies that build."
  • "Your competitor's Instagram is their best recruiter. Is yours?"
  • "One filming day. 30 days of content. Zero guesswork."
  • "We don't make videos. We build systems that use video."

7. What Changes from Current Site

Keep

  • Dark background foundation (shifting warmer, not lighter)
  • #E85D26 orange as primary accent
  • Heavy italic uppercase headlines (the most distinctive visual element)
  • Mono-spaced micro-labels and category tags
  • The scramble text effect (unique, on-brand)
  • The typewriter cycle effect in the hero
  • Noise/grain texture overlay
  • Testimonial card structure (metric badge + quote + attribution)
  • Video module hover behavior (grayscale to color, slight scale)
  • The form flow approach (structured brief, not just "contact us")

Kill

  • "Phoenix Video Production" positioning anywhere on site
  • "Founders/developers/SaaS" as stated audience
  • Engagement idea names: "The Big Launch", "The Wildcard", "Founder Authority" (too generic, too cute)
  • The trust logos ticker with generic industry words (INDUSTRIAL, CONSTRUCTION, etc.). Either show real client logos or remove entirely.
  • The bottom ticker/scroll bar
  • "Call Rentals" phone number
  • Cool zinc color palette (replace with warm stone/neutral system above)
  • three.js import (loaded but never used, 162KB dead weight)
  • Single-file App.jsx architecture (979 lines, no routing)

Add

  • Services grid with three clear lanes (Content Engine, Production, Digital Infrastructure)
  • Construction-specific section or callout (Ambition Mechanical as proof point)
  • AI/systems teaser section with waitlist (sage green accent, mono typography, show the engine)
  • Case study pages (not just video embeds, but full story + metrics + tags)
  • SEO basics: meta tags, OG tags, structured data
  • Real client logos in trust section (with permission) or remove the section entirely
  • "See What We'd Build For You" as the primary CTA language
  • React Router + component architecture (Bobby's first technical task)

Implementation Notes for Bobby

  1. Start with Tailwind config. Drop the color and font configs from sections 2 and 3 into tailwind.config.js before touching any components.
  2. Font imports go in index.html or the CSS entry point. All three Google Fonts imports.
  3. Replace zinc- classes with aom- custom classes throughout. This is the biggest visual shift and can be done with find-and-replace after the Tailwind config is set.
  4. The warm shift is subtle. Night (#0C0C0C) vs pure black, Text Light (#F0ECE6) vs pure white. The difference is felt more than seen. That's the point.
  5. Sage green sections are isolated to AI/systems content. Don't bleed sage into other sections. Orange is still the dominant accent everywhere else.
  6. Component patterns above are guidelines, not rigid templates. If a component needs to flex for content, flex it. But the type hierarchy, color roles, and spacing philosophy are non-negotiable.

This document is the source of truth for AOM's visual identity. All agents (Bobby, Cleo, Tony) reference this before shipping anything AOM-facing. Patrik reviews before implementation begins.
